      "quote": "God could provide such evidence selectively only to persons who he knew would respond to it",
      "form": "no",

He requires evidence for willing responders and separately argues that public evidence exists (E1040-E1063), leaving unrestricted protection uncertain."
    },

      "contextEndEvent": 2651,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "the evil and suffering the world I think does not render improbable the existence of the Christian God",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": [
        "none"
      ],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Craig asserts that suffering does not make Christian theism improbable but postpones the supporting explanation to published work (E2643-E2651). Unspecified divine reasons might protect the claim, yet E2619-E2634 explicitly distinguishes logical compatibility from probability. No unrestricted compensation or intention is supplied that demonstrably neutralizes every contrary pattern."
    }
  ],

      "quote": "while we cannot prove that the Universe came about in this exact manner",
      "explanation": "Stenger distinguishes a proposed natural mechanism from an established actual history. Following the tunneling discussion at E741-E760, he limits the inference to whether supernatural explanation is required. The qualification gives this concise conclusion substantive context rather than using it as an unsupported slogan."
    },
